gaps.sentence: Take a jumper ___ the evening turns cold.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against possibility.

gaps.sentence: He spends money ___ it grew on trees.
gaps.explanation: 'As if it grew on trees' — the unreal comparison justifies the criticism.
'Due to personal reasons' is the standard collocation for giving a cause.

gaps.sentence: ___ you book soon, there won't be any seats left.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if... not': if you don't book soon, no seats.

gaps.sentence: ___ was the meal exquisite, but the service was impeccable too.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only' at the front triggers inversion (Not only was...) and pairs with 'but also'.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: ___ he had studied hard, he failed the exam.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a full clause; due/owing take noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.
